key_insight: Engineering the ferroelectric domain pattern in BiFeO3 thin films controls both the strength and origin of bias-free THz emission, with stripe domains giving the strongest output.
engineering_relevance: Domain design is a practical tuning knob for efficient, voltage-free THz sources, enabling stronger emission without the external bias or magnetic field required by conventional emitters.
method: Compared epitaxial BiFeO3 thin films with single-domain and periodic stripe-domain configurations.
Measured emitted THz fields versus pump polarization and crystal orientation in amplitude and phase.
Separated photocurrent contributions by symmetry to identify the dominant emission mechanism.
evidence_signal: The stripe-domain film produced a THz field about 4× stronger than single-domain films and reached roughly half the output of a metallic spintronic reference while remaining unsaturated at the highest fluences.
watch_item: The strongest performance depends on precise ferroelectric domain engineering, so reproducibility and domain stability during growth and operation are key implementation challenges.
paper_title: Domain-engineered ferroelectric BiFeO$_3$ thin films for efficient bias-free THz emission
